final_recommendation: The room converged on a concrete, operationalized risk framework: Supplier A (14.2% RVC gap) triggers immediate nearshoring; Suppliers B and C enter 90-day re-qualification with day-30 file-audit and day-45 logistics checkpoints gating credit restructuring and capex decisions. A $300K parallel nearshoring prep for Supplier B hedges against 65% probability of CBP audit acceleration (days 45-70), with all exposures priced into a unified supplier risk matrix.

key_concessions: CFO accepted $300K sunk-cost exposure on parallel nearshoring prep for Supplier B as acceptable insurance against mid-cycle supplier failure
Trade credit underwriter accepted front-loading payment-term concession for Supplier B to mitigate 12% default probability under audit acceleration
Political risk insurer accepted 15% enforcement-escalation buffer as sufficient for penalty exposure but not working-capital strain, forcing payment restructure decision
red_lines: 12% landed-cost threshold (penalty + capex) as hard trigger for nearshoring vs. re-qualification

No simultaneous nearshoring of more than two supplier categories due to $2-4M capex and 6-9 month qualification lead time constraints

Retroactive penalty exposure on shipments already flagged during re-qualification window mentioned but not integrated into materiality ranking
